author: Inside Edition
description: An Arkansas family was shocked to discover that someone had been sleeping in their basement. Mark Gregory's in-laws noticed things were off when stuff was being moved around, and food kept going missing. Eventually, Mark and his family checked the basement and discovered that a man had been there for several days following what he said was a mental health emergency. Inside Edition Digital's Andrea Swindal has more.
title: Arkansas Family Discovers Man Living In Basement

author: Inside Edition
description: A giant crocodile swam right in front of two models during an underwater photo shoot. Kimber Kiefer says she was with her husband Ken, a professional underwater photographer, shooting pictures with another model when the crocodile calmly swam up to them. Crocodiles are known for their long powerful jaws, sharp teeth and terrifying death rolls. Fortunately, the crocodile that swam past the photoshoot is a local celebrity in Casa Cenota, Mexico and is known to be relatively docile.
title: Crocodile Swims In Front Of Two Models During Photoshoot

author: Inside Edition
description: There is a new trend celebrating brides-to-be: the no-booze bachelorette party. Madeline Durso and her bridesmaids think it's great. They partook in goat yoga and ran a bachelorette 5k race. The party then relaxed for massages and pedicures. Instead of sipping cocktails, they enjoyed fresh juice at "A Garden Party" in Elmer, New Jersey. "We wanted to do something out of the box," Durso tells Inside Edition. The entire day was planned by Renee Patrone Rhinehart, founder of Events By Renee.
title: Booze-Free Bachelorette Celebrations On The Rise

author: Inside Edition
description: Officials say a sheriff's deputy in Florida was saved by his bullet proof vest when a suspect attacked him with a knife. The Marion County Sheriff released video of the incident. After rushing the deputy and hitting him on the ground, the suspect fled into the woods while the deputy called for backup. When other deputies arrived, the suspect emerged from the woods and surrendered. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Suspect Tells Deputy 'I Should Have Killed You' After Knife Attack

author: Inside Edition
description: Are these birds guardians of the past? In a way, yes, according to scientists in Spain. They tell CBS News the bearded vulture hasn't inhabited the Sierra Nevada Mountains in quite some time, but the nests they left behind contain valuable information. The fact that these birds of prey nested in caves helped preserve the interesting items they used to pad their nests. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Scientists Say Nests Of Bearded Vultures Contain Many Clues To The Past

title: Plane Nearly Crashes Into Car On Highway #shorts
